On success, the response returns the updated DiscussionBoardModerationAppeal entity, reflecting the post-update state. Errors return standard API error types for not found, forbidden, or invalid update attempts. Any field changes are logged according to platform audit policy.

IDiscussionBoardPolicyChangeLogs.IUpdate.description:
Discussion Board Policy Change Log Update Type

This schema defines the structure for updating an existing policy change log entry in the Discussion Board platform. Policy change logs serve as an immutable audit trail for all changes to content policies or business rules, establishing traceability and compliance for platform governance. This update type must capture who made the change (admin), what type of change was performed (edit, correction, etc.), the before/after JSON state (for full transparency and potential rollback), and the timestamp for audit chronology.

All fields map to the underlying Prisma DB schema (`discussionboard_policy_change_logs`), referencing policy, rule, actor admin, and change event details. Nullability and required status strictly follow schema constraints to ensure completeness for audit and compliance workflows. created_at.description: Timestamp when action was created/recorded (ISO8601, stored as Prisma DateTime @db.Timestamptz).

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.description: Moderation action entity recording a single action performed by a moderator/admin on content or members. Represents an auditable, atomic event (edit, warning, ban, reinstatement, etc.) and stores links to actors (moderator/admin), affected content, and justification. Reflects Prisma model discussionboard_moderation_actions. Relationships system-enforced; refer to related member/content when populating references.

oneOf.description: ID of the moderator performing the action; required if action is from moderator, nullable if from admin. Must match discussionboard_moderators.id. (Required relationship in business context, nullable schema in DB/prisma).

ID of the moderator performing the action; required if action is from moderator, nullable if from admin. Must match discussionboard_moderators.id. (Required relationship in business context, nullable schema in DB/prisma).

moderator_id.description: ID of the moderator performing the action; required if action is from moderator, nullable if from admin. Must match discussionboard_moderators.id. (Required relationship in business context, nullable schema in DB/prisma).

oneOf.description: ID of the admin performing the action; for admin-direct actions only. Mutable if moderator is acting, and vice versa. Must match discussionboard_admins.id.
ID of the admin performing the action; for admin-direct actions only. Mutable if moderator is acting, and vice versa. Must match discussionboard_admins.id.

admin_id.description: ID of the admin performing the action; for admin-direct actions only. Mutable if moderator is acting, and vice versa. Must match discussionboard_admins.id.

oneOf.description: ID of the post that is the subject of the action (e.g., removed, edited). May be null for comment/member actions.
ID of the post that is the subject of the action (e.g., removed, edited). May be null for comment/member actions.

target_post_id.description: ID of the post that is the subject of the action (e.g., removed, edited). May be null for comment/member actions.

oneOf.description: ID of the comment that is the subject of the action. May be null for post/member-only actions.
ID of the comment that is the subject of the action. May be null for post/member-only actions.

target_comment_id.description: ID of the comment that is the subject of the action. May be null for post/member-only actions.

affected_member_id.description: ID of the member subject to moderation. Not nullable - required in all action creation.

action_type.description: Action type to be recorded (e.g., 'edit', 'warn', 'suspend'). Should match business rules/allowed values for reporting. Stored as atomic string.

action_reason.description: Justification, main rationale, or audit reason for this moderation action. Required free text, used by audit and appeal workflows.

oneOf.description: Additional context or moderator/admin note. Optional, nullable for extra audit/comment context.
Additional context or moderator/admin note. Optional, nullable for extra audit/comment context.

action_note.description: Additional context or moderator/admin note. Optional, nullable for extra audit/comment context.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ICreate.description: Creation payload for moderation action entries. Used by backend, moderator/admin tools to log moderation/compliance steps in the audit trail, acting upon content/member as per business needs. Fields must be normalized, point to valid actor/content as per foreign keys in Prisma schema.

oneOf.description: (Optional) Updated moderator actor (for correction scenarios only). Usually immutable, but allowed in exceptional admin flows.
(Optional) Updated moderator actor (for correction scenarios only). Usually immutable, but allowed in exceptional admin flows.

moderator_id.description: (Optional) Updated moderator actor (for correction scenarios only). Usually immutable, but allowed in exceptional admin flows.

oneOf.description: (Optional) Updated admin actor (for correction scenarios).
(Optional) Updated admin actor (for correction scenarios).
Updated post target (if action is being corrected to reference a different post).
Updated post target (if action is being corrected to reference a different post).

target_post_id.description: Updated post target (if action is being corrected to reference a different post).

oneOf.description: Updated comment target (if correction made to reference different comment).
Updated comment target (if correction made to reference different comment).

target_comment_id.description: Updated comment target (if correction made to reference different comment).

affected_member_id.description: Updated affected member (correction only). Use with caution—rarely editable in audit-correct flows.

action_type.description: Updated action type if revision required.

action_reason.description: Modified reason or justification for the action (correction flow; uncommon).

oneOf.description: Amended additional context/note (rarely changes post-creation).
Amended additional context/note (rarely changes post-creation).

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.IUpdate.description: Update structure for correcting moderation action logs/records. Optional fields as correction is a rare, privileged admin flow. All fields are mutable in this interface for exceptional business/audit scenarios; never update from normal moderation panel. Edits should be tracked with full audit trail for compliance.

page.description: Pagination - result page number.

limit.description: Pagination - results per page.

moderation_action_id.description: Filter by appealed moderation action (ID; links to moderation action entity).

member_id.description: Filter by member/appellant who filed the appeal.

appeal_status.description: Filter by current appeal status (e.g., 'pending', 'decided', 'withdrawn', etc.)

created_at_from.description: Filter for appeals created at or after (ISO 8601).

created_at_to.description: Filter for appeals created at or before (ISO 8601).

IDiscussionBoardModerationAppeal.IReques.description: Object for filtering and searching moderation appeals in admin and moderator interfaces. All fields are optional and intended for UI-driven query building. Matching structure for appeals data in discussionboard_moderation_appeals and related dashboard/reporting contexts.

IDiscussionBoardPost.description:
Discussion Board Post Entity.

Represents a user-generated post (thread starter) in a discussion board. This schema directly models the 'discussionboard_posts' table in the Prisma DB schema, capturing all atomic properties including relational references, content, moderation states, and audit timestamps.

Business context: Posts are authored by members and belong to a specific board. They support full revision, deletion, locking, and view-tracking, and are integrated with moderation, analytics, and content feeds. This core type is the cornerstone of discussion content in the platform, supporting all board, comment, and moderation features described in the requirements analysis.

id.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies this post. Generated as a UUID for distributed consistency and audit traceability. Maps to the 'id' field in Prisma DB.

board_id.description: Board reference. The UUID of the board (discussionboard_boards.id) this post is associated with. Enforces organizational structure.

author_id.description: Author reference. The UUID of the authoring member (discussionboard_members.id).

title.description: Post headline. A short, concise summary/title of the post—user-supplied. Required. Stored normalized.

body.description: Main post content. Markdown/text body provided by user. Required. No derived or summary content.

view_count.description: Count of unique or total views on this post. Used for engagement analytics. Not an aggregated value, only carries atomic view count.

is_locked.description: Thread lock flag. True if the post is currently locked and not open to edits or new comments. Supports moderation and business rules.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, in ISO 8601 format. Recorded for ordering, display, and audit trails.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, ISO 8601 format. Used for concurrency control and activity monitoring.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If set, indicates the post is deleted but auditable/recoverable. Null if active.
Soft-delete timestamp. If set, indicates the post is deleted but auditable/recoverable. Null if active.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If set, indicates the post is deleted but auditable/recoverable. Null if active.

IDiscussionBoardPost.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new Discussion Board Post (thread).

Defines fields needed for POST operations to create a post, corresponding to insertions into the 'discussionboard_posts' table. Details are validated, and some fields (like timestamps, view_count, is_locked, id) may be auto-generated server-side.

board_id.description: Board reference. Required; post will be associated with the referenced board.

author_id.description: Author reference. Required. The UUID of the member creating the post.

title.description: Title for the post, short summary. Must comply with content policies.

body.description: Main content of the post. Must comply with length and moderation policies.

IDiscussionBoardPost.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing Discussion Board Post.

Model for PUT/PATCH operations on discussionboard_posts. Not all fields may be updatable at once. This variant allows partial updates; fields provided are changed, others are left untouched. Validation rules maintain content and audit compliance; only permitted actors may perform updates.

title.description: Updated post title. Optional. Must comply with naming/content policies.

is_locked.description: Thread lock flag. If true, closes post for further edits/comments.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Setting to non-null marks the post as deleted (soft delete), leaving for audit/history. Optional.
Soft-delete timestamp. Setting to non-null marks the post as deleted (soft delete), leaving for audit/history. Optional.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Setting to non-null marks the post as deleted (soft delete), leaving for audit/history. Optional.

IDiscussionBoardPostEdit.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching and paginating post edit log entities.

Used in PATCH /discussionBoard/postEdits endpoint: allows filtering on post edits by fields such as post/ref IDs, editor, date ranges. Supports full audit and moderation review workflows for post revision history.

post_id.description: Filter by unique ID of the target post. Optional.

editor_id.description: Filter by member who made the edit. Optional.

created_from.description: Lower bound filter for edit creation datetime. Optional.

created_to.description: Upper bound filter for edit creation datetime. Optional.

page.description: Paginated page index. Optional.

limit.description: Page size (number of records per page). Optional.

IPageIDiscussionBoardPostEdit.description:
Paginated page of Discussion Board Post Edit entities, adhering to platform's paging conventions.

Combines metadata necessary for implementing UI navigation, bulk editing, and large result sets for audit or moderator review. Used as response for PATCH /discussionBoard/postEdits.

pagination.description: Paging information. Contains current page, limit, total records, and total pages.

data.description: List of post edit log records for current page.

IDiscussionBoardPostEdit.description:
Edit log entity for Discussion Board Post.

Captures a single revision event for a post, as per the 'discussionboard_post_edits' Prisma model. Enables audit trails, moderation dispute review, and rollback capabilities. Each edit records which post was changed, by whom, the updated content, and relevant timestamps/history details.

id.description: Primary key for the edit event. Unique ID for this edit log entry.

post_id.description: Target Post. The post whose content is being edited; foreign key to discussionboard_posts.id.

editor_id.description: Editor. UUID of member who performed the edit (author/moderator/admin).

oneOf.description: (Optional) Short explanation or rationale for the edit, aiding moderator review. E.g., 'corrected typo'. Null if not specified.
(Optional) Short explanation or rationale for the edit, aiding moderator review. E.g., 'corrected typo'. Null if not specified.

edit_summary.description: (Optional) Short explanation or rationale for the edit, aiding moderator review. E.g., 'corrected typo'. Null if not specified.

body_after_edit.description: Full content of the post AFTER the edit. Provides post-edit snapshot for audit/history.

created_at.description: Timestamp when edit was performed, for chronological audit trails.

IDiscussionBoardPostEdit.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a Discussion Board Post Edit log.

Input structure for recording a new post edit event, as required by audit, moderation, and revision history features. Timestamps, and unique IDs are generally generated server-side.

Business rules may enforce who can submit edits and when; must correspond to changes in the referenced post entity.

post_id.description: Target Post UUID. Required. The post being changed.

oneOf.description: Edit summary or rationale. Optional but recommended for moderator clarity.
Edit summary or rationale. Optional but recommended for moderator clarity.

edit_summary.description: Edit summary or rationale. Optional but recommended for moderator clarity.

IDiscussionBoardPostEdit.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating a Post Edit log entry on the Discussion Board.

Enables partial update of editable fields—mainly correction or supplement of edit summary, or update to post body under permitted business logic. Authorisation and field-level validation applies. Timestamps are updated as needed; IDs/post/editor links are immutable.

oneOf.description: (Optional) Corrected or supplemented edit rationale.
(Optional) Corrected or supplemented edit rationale.

IDiscussionBoardPostSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching and paginating Discussion Board Post Snapshot entities.

Used by PATCH /discussionBoard/postSnapshots endpoint to query version timelines for posts, filtering by post, creator, timespan, etc. Supports full history navigation and audit/query workflows.

post_id.description: Filter by post UUID. Optional for full listing.

created_by_id.description: Filter by creator member UUID. Optional.

created_from.description: Lower bound filter for snapshot creation date.

created_to.description: Upper bound filter for snapshot date.

page.description: Paging: page index. Optional.

limit.description: Paging: records per page. Optional.

IPageIDiscussionBoardPostSnapshot.description:
Page of Discussion Board Post Snapshots, supporting full platform paging for history/audit UIs.

Response for PATCH /discussionBoard/postSnapshots, integrating result objects and metadata for navigation/scalability.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata (page #, limit, total, pages, etc).

data.description: List of snapshot entries on this page.

IPageIDiscussionBoardPostSnapshot.$comment: Standard paging result for history lists.

IDiscussionBoardPostSnapshot.description:
Discussion Board Post Snapshot entity.

Stores a frozen, point-in-time record of a post's content and title for audit, rollback, and moderator/legal reference. Snapshots capture the full state of the post at key revision/time points, fulfilling business requirements for transparency and dispute resolution.

Used by platform rollback, history, and compliance/audit features. Mapped directly to the Prisma DB schema discussionboard_post_snapshots.

id.description: Primary key for this snapshot (unique UUID).

post_id.description: Parent post's UUID, references discussionboard_posts.id.

created_by_id.description: Member UUID who created the snapshot.

title.description: Snapshot of post's title at snapshotted time (no aggregation).

body.description: Snapshot of post content/body at that time.

created_at.description: When the snapshot was created. ISO 8601 format.

IDiscussionBoardPostSnapshot.ICreate.description:
Create request schema for Discussion Board Post Snapshot entity.

Submitted to create a new point-in-time backup of a post, used for critical revision, legal hold, or moderation/rollback workflows. Must supply post, creator, and content fields; other fields are generated server-side.

post_id.description: Target post's UUID (snapshot subject). Required.

created_by_id.description: Snapshot creator's UUID, usually the actor recording or intervening.

title.description: Full title at snapshot time, for display/history.

body.description: Full post body at snapshot time.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Paging metadata for paginated result containers, compliant with project paging conventions and IPage<T> pattern.

Contains record count, total pages, current page, and per-page limit to support UI navigation and scalable queries.

limit.description: Number of items per page (page size).

records.description: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description: Total page count. Equals ceil(records / limit).

title.description:
The title of the post as captured in this snapshot.

This field is mandatory when updating a post snapshot. It holds the user-facing summary and is kept atomic in line with the system's normalization requirements. Refer to the original Prisma schema for business rules: must be concise but sufficiently descriptive for historical review and auditability.

body.description:
The main content body as of the post's snapshot update.

Must include the full markdown or plain text body as it was at the snapshot event. Per the 3NF business rule, this is a complete version with no aggregation or derived values. Used for audits, rollback, and dispute resolution. See DB schema and documentation on required normalization.

IDiscussionBoardPostSnapshot.IUpdate.description:
Update type for a discussion board post snapshot.

Allows authorized actors to perform corrections or amendments to a previously archived post state record. All fields are required for auditability. Properties correspond directly to the atomic post fields as of the snapshot. Follows strict domain normalization, auditability, and compliance requirements as described in the requirement analysis and Prisma schema documentation.

post_id.description:
The unique identifier of the post to filter comments for.

Optional. If provided, restricts returned results to comments under a specific discussion post. This supports UI comment threading as well as moderation review targeting a particular post. Follows normalized use of post association per DB schema.

thread_id.description:
The thread identifier to filter comments by thread.

Optional. When set, retrieves only comments associated with the specified thread. This enables advanced search/filter by nested structure in threaded discussions. Defined in the ERD as comment-to-thread mapping.

author_id.description:
Retricts search to comments created by this member's unique UUID.

Optional. Used for member history, analytics, or moderation requests. 3NF property from the comment schema.

body_text.description:
Search string to filter comments by fulltext or substring match of the comment body.

Optional. Respects business rules for privacy, search visibility, and compliance.

depth_min.description:
Minimum nesting depth for returned comments.

Optional. Depth values align with comment threading and moderation hierarchy per the requirements analysis.

depth_max.description:
Maximum nesting depth for filtered search results.

Optional. Controls retrieval by nesting, e.g., for root comments or deeply nested replies.

created_at_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for creation date of comments returned.

Optional. Must be formatted as an ISO8601 timestamp.

created_at_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for creation date of comments returned.

Optional. Must be formatted as an ISO8601 timestamp.

updated_at_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for last update date of comments.

Optional. ISO8601 timestamp required.

updated_at_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for last update date of comments.

Optional. ISO8601 timestamp required.

is_edited.description:
Filter by whether comments have been edited.

Optional. True for edited, false for never-edited comments. Follows moderation and transparency rules documented in the requirements analysis.

is_deleted.description:
Filter by comment deletion (soft-deleted) status.

Optional. True returns only deleted comments, false returns active/non-deleted comments. Handles moderation view workflows. See DB schema for soft-delete handling.

sort.description:
Sort order for results, typically one of 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'depth', possibly with direction (asc/desc).

Optional. Reflects UI and compliance needs for result ordering.

page.description:
Pagination parameter - 1-based page number.

Optional. Used for paginated result views as per the IPage container.

limit.description:
Maximum comments to return per page.

Optional. Follows pagination business logic.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Request type for searching and filtering comments in the discussion board.

Enables advanced query support for moderation, UI rendering, or analytics, using atomic normalized filtering by post, thread, author, content, depth, timestamps, and deletion status. Optionality provides flexibility, and all properties match system design rules for filtering per normalized domain as described in the requirements analysis.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the comments result set.

Contains total records, current page, page size, and page count as per the requirements documentation.

data.description:
List of comments on the current page, as detailed atomic entities.

Each entry is a normalized comment record, following the business and technical requirements from the analysis.

IPageIDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Paginated container for comment entities in the Discussion Board.

Encapsulates a result set of comments matched by a search or filter query, together with page-level metadata as per domain rules for UI consumption and analytics. Implements the IPage container standard for the platform.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the comment entity.

Primary key per DB schema and 3NF, referenced throughout the system for reply, reaction, and moderation workflows.

post_id.description:
ID of the post to which this comment belongs.

Links comments to the context of a discussion thread, enforcing business and technical integrity as defined in the schema.

thread_id.description:
ID of the comment thread (conversation branch) this comment is associated with.

Used for nesting structure, reply context, and analytics. Refer to the detailed comment threading strategy in requirements and ERD.

author_id.description:
UUID of the member who authored the comment.

Referenced for attribution, permissions, and moderation. Normalized for historical trace and business logic.

body.description:
Textual body/content of the comment.

Required for every comment per system rules, stored in markdown or plain text format per the platform specification. Fully atomic and non-derived.

depth.description:
Nesting depth of the comment in its thread.

0 = root level, higher for nested replies. See threading strategy in requirements, used for UI/analytics.

is_edited.description:
Whether this comment has been edited since creation.

Required for compliance & transparency, linked to the comment_edits table in the DB.

created_at.description:
When the comment was created, as an ISO8601 timestamp.

For audit trail and UI sorting as required by requirements analysis.

updated_at.description:
When the comment was last updated (even if not edited).

Traces all changes for compliance and moderation workflows.

oneOf.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp if the comment is marked deleted.

Null if not deleted, otherwise set to the ISO8601 deletion time. Used in moderation, audit, and compliance as described in the business rules.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp if the comment is marked deleted.

Null if not deleted, otherwise set to the ISO8601 deletion time. Used in moderation, audit, and compliance as described in the business rules.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Atomic, normalized schema for a discussion board comment entity.

Represents user-generated comment content in a threaded conversation, including all business-critical and compliance metadata as described in requirements analysis and the Prisma schema documentation. Required for UI rendering, moderation, thread analytics, and audit trail.

post_id.description:
ID of the post to attach the new comment to.

Required. Must point to an existing, active post as defined in the business rules.

thread_id.description:
Thread identifier to which the comment belongs (may be a root or sub-thread).

Required. Correct threading is critical for business logic and UI structure.

author_id.description:
UUID for the member creating this comment.

Required for attribution and audit. Must be an active, authenticated member.

body.description:
Content text of the new comment.

Required and must pass business and moderation policy checks for permitted content (e.g., length, prohibited language, etc.).

depth.description:
Nesting depth of the new comment.

Required. 0 for root, increase for replies. See threading policy for allowed values.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Creation request type for a new comment in Discussion Board.

Used to submit a new comment entity, following all required rules for thread association, authoring member, nesting, and platform moderation as covered in the requirements analysis and DB schema. Ensures all fields are normalized for downstream analytics and audit.

body.description:
Updated body/content for the comment.

Must conform to platform business rules (e.g., prohibited content checks, length).

is_edited.description:
Flag to set or clear the edited state for the comment, indicating whether the body has been changed after creation.

Business rules enforce transparency and edit history compliance.

oneOf.description:
Optional update to soft-delete the comment (ISO8601 format).

Null or missing means not deleted; set to timestamp for deletion as per audit/business policies.

deleted_at.description:
Optional update to soft-delete the comment (ISO8601 format).

Null or missing means not deleted; set to timestamp for deletion as per audit/business policies.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Update mutation type for a comment in the Discussion Board.

Allows the author, moderator, or admin to modify comment content, set edit flag, or soft-delete (for compliance). Follows all business logic for field updateability and audit trail as in the requirements and DB schema.

success.description:
Indicates whether the deletion operation succeeded.

True if successfully deleted (or soft-deleted), false otherwise. Used for API responses across the discussion board platform domains.

message.description:
Explanatory message conveying the result of the deletion operation.

May include reason for failure, confirmation text, or audit tracking information as required by business compliance rules.

IDeleteResult.description:
Standard result schema for a deletion operation outcome (success/failure, optional message).

Used by DELETE operations across discussion board entities for confirmation in compliance and audit workflows.

post_id.description:
Filter: only return threads for this post ID.

Optional. Enables selective construction of comment trees per post according to requirements.

parent_thread_id.description:
Filter: restricts threads to those below this parent (i.e., nested threads).

Optional. Used for detailed hierarchical UI crawling or moderation sub-thread review.

depth_min.description:
Lower bound for thread depth to filter (inclusive).

Optional. Allows fetching only root or only subthreads as per UI/analytics.

depth_max.description:
Upper bound for thread depth to filter (inclusive).

Optional.

created_at_from.description:
Earliest creation timestamp filter for returned threads.

Optional. Must be ISO8601 per audit policy and technical schema.

created_at_to.description:
Latest creation timestamp filter for returned threads.

Optional. ISO8601 as above.

sort.description:
Sorting property and direction, e.g. 'created_at desc', for ordering returned threads.

Optional. Mirrors UI and audit analytics business requirements.

page.description:
Pagination - 1-based page number for thread results.

Optional. Used for efficient tree navigation.

limit.description:
Max number of threads to return per page.

Optional. Follows system default and business logic for UI.

IDiscussionBoardCommentThread.IRequest.description:
Request type for querying comment thread entities in the Discussion Board.

Supports the requirements for advanced filtering of hierarchical threads for UI, analytics, and moderation navigations, based on normalized, atomic schema mapping. Aligns exactly with ERD and requirements analysis for thread search and crawl.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for comment thread search results.

Includes page info, total count, per-page count, current position as required by audit, analytics, and UI needs.

data.description:
Comment thread entries retrieved for this page of results.

Consists of normalized atomic thread records following Content domain schema requirements.

IPageIDiscussionBoardCommentThread.description:
Paginated container type for comment thread entities in Discussion Board.

Implements IPage contract for returning search/browse results with full pagination info and list of normalized thread entries per technical/business requirements.

id.description:
Unique comment thread identifier (primary key).

Links threads to posts and manages parent/child thread trees for Content domain. Required by ERD and audit rules.

post_id.description:
ID of the post that this thread belongs to.

Critical for linking root and subthreads to post contexts in the platform. Enforces integrity.

oneOf.description:
Parent thread UUID if this is a subthread; null for root threads.

Provides full traceability for tree navigation and moderation/analytics. See thread parent-child structure in Content ERD.

parent_thread_id.description:
Parent thread UUID if this is a subthread; null for root threads.

Provides full traceability for tree navigation and moderation/analytics. See thread parent-child structure in Content ERD.

depth.description:
Nesting or hierarchy depth of this thread.

Root threads are depth 0, incrementing for each nesting level. Used for thread analytics and UI rendering in compliance with requirements logic.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this thread was created (ISO8601).

Critical for structural audits, moderation review, and analytics workflow.

IDiscussionBoardCommentThread.description:
Atomic schema for a comment thread entity in Discussion Board.

Defines root and nested thread structures for organizing comments per post, according to normalized business logic as described in requirements and DB documentation. Used for tree traversal, moderation, analytics, and UI context presentation.

post_id.description:
The post ID this thread is associated with.

Required for creation. Only valid for existing, non-deleted posts, as mandated by DB schema and requirements.

oneOf.description:
Parent thread ID for a nested (child) thread, or null if a root thread.

Enforces parent/child thread structure in line with Content model and UI requirements.

parent_thread_id.description:
Parent thread ID for a nested (child) thread, or null if a root thread.

Enforces parent/child thread structure in line with Content model and UI requirements.

depth.description:
The depth of this thread in the tree (0=root, >0 for nested).

Enforces threading UI, moderation, and analytics as required by business logic.

IDiscussionBoardCommentThread.ICreate.description:
Creation type for a new comment thread entity in Discussion Board.

Supports the technical and business rules for constructing root threads and subthreads under posts, as implemented in the normalized ERD and described in the requirements documentation.

oneOf.description:
New parent thread ID for the updated thread. Null if becoming a root thread.

Updates thread structure, enforcing business policy for valid nesting and compliance with thread parent-child mapping from the ERD.

parent_thread_id.description:
New parent thread ID for the updated thread. Null if becoming a root thread.

Updates thread structure, enforcing business policy for valid nesting and compliance with thread parent-child mapping from the ERD.

depth.description:
Updated depth of the thread, if necessary.

Enforces hierarchy consistency and system rules for thread repointing or tree-correction actions. Must follow allowed nesting limits.

IDiscussionBoardCommentThread.IUpdate.description:
Update type for a comment thread in Discussion Board.

Permits changing the nesting, parent-child relationship, or depth for moderation and structural repair as covered by the requirements and ER diagram.

limit.description: Number of records per page.

records.description: Total number of records in result set.

pages.description: Total number of pages in result set.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Standard page metadata type used by all IPage containers.

Tracks the state of paginated result sets across the API for discussion board and all platform domains.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for each configuration parameter row. From the Prisma schema: audit, rollback, and historical tracking if paired with snapshots.

Business meaning: Uniquely distinguishes each configuration for retrieval, update, and compliance tracking.

key.description: Configuration key name. Implements requirement for system parameterization. Atomic: e.g., 'max_post_length'.

value.description: Configuration value. Business meaning: stores the override for the specified key. Fully atomic; no derived/pre-computed data allowed.

oneOf.description: Description or purpose of this configuration parameter, for documentation. Optional, remains atomic and normalized.

description.description: Description or purpose of this configuration parameter, for documentation. Optional, remains atomic and normalized.

created_at.description: Timestamp of parameter creation. Supports requirement for modification audit trail.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of most recent modification. Enables accurate tracking and rollback if required.

oneOf.description: If filled, records parameter soft deletion timestamp. Maintains auditability for deleted entries.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.description:

code.description:
The unique short string identifier code for the content policy. Maps to the 'code' column in the discussionboard_content_policies table. This identifier is used system-wide to reference the policy during report logging, moderation, and audit. The code must be unique and may reference business requirements such as 'GENERAL', 'SPAM', or 'HATE_SPEECH'.

Multiple paragraphs may include how the code facilitates rapid lookup and categorizations of content policies in both admin dashboards and automated enforcement logic.

title.description:
Human-readable title of the policy. Maps to the 'title' column in the discussionboard_content_policies table. Provides a user-facing summary of the policy such as 'No Hate Speech' or 'No Spam'.

This property aids in UI rendering and administrative referencing of policy context, especially as guidelines are updated over time.

description.description:
Full policy text or markdown, mapping directly to the 'description' column in content policies. Contains the detailed rules, examples, and explanations of the policy as required for platform transparency and enforcement.

Detailed policy descriptions guide both user behavior and moderator actions during enforcement and are critical for dispute resolution and platform audits.

effective_from.description: Date and time as of which the policy becomes effective. Maps to the 'effective_from' column. Used to version and time-scope rulesets, enabling compliance reporting and historical review of rule application.

oneOf.description: Expiration or withdrawal date/time for the policy (optional). Maps to 'effective_to'. When set, indicates the endpoint for enforcement of this guideline. Null means policy is current. Useful for deprecating or superseding policies as regulations change.

Expiration or withdrawal date/time for the policy (optional). Maps to 'effective_to'. When set, indicates the endpoint for enforcement of this guideline. Null means policy is current. Useful for deprecating or superseding policies as regulations change.

effective_to.description: Expiration or withdrawal date/time for the policy (optional). Maps to 'effective_to'. When set, indicates the endpoint for enforcement of this guideline. Null means policy is current. Useful for deprecating or superseding policies as regulations change.

is_active.description: Indicates if the policy is currently enforced. Maps to 'is_active' DB column. True means the policy is in effect and visible to users/moderators; false deactivates the policy for future enforcement. Used by admin for maintenance or withdrawal procedures.

DiscussionBoardContentPolicies.IUpdate.description:
This schema represents the updatable fields for a content policy in the Discussion Board context, as mapped from the discussionboard_content_policies Prisma model. It is used for updating policy records through admin workflows. Each property aligns with normalization and audit requirements described in the requirements analysis and is referenced directly in audit logs and UI displays.

Each property maps precisely to its respective column in the database, ensuring that all revisions are traceable for compliance and rollback. The schema reflects best practices for transparency, enforcement, and dynamic rule adjustment within a large-scale discussion platform.

key.description: Optional. Filter results by unique key identifier such as 'MAX_POST_LENGTH', 'ALLOW_EDIT', etc. Used for search/scoping in discussionboard_business_rules table.

value.description: Optional. Filter by value. The value represents the parameterization (e.g., '10000' for max post length or 'true' for an enable toggle).

description.description: Optional. Search by rule description. Useful for admin UI text search or advanced audit queries.

page.description: Optional. Results page to fetch for pagination. 1-indexed.

limit.description: Optional. Page size limit for paginated result sets.

DiscussionBoardBusinessRules.IRequest.description: Request parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating business rules in the Discussion Board system. Each property provides a filter constraint for the search operation, enabling flexible and efficient querying. The schema is designed for use in admin panels, compliance tools, and automation scripts as defined in the requirements report.

data.description: Array of business rule objects as returned by the search.

DiscussionBoardPageBusinessRules.description:
A paginated set of business rules for the Discussion Board system, corresponding to the IPage<T> container defined in the requirements analysis. This schema is used for returning results to clients requesting filtered or paginated business rules as part of administrative or compliance workflows.

Contains both the pagination metadata and the array of rule objects as defined by IDiscussionBoardBusinessRules.

id.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies each business rule row in the discussionboard_business_rules table. Used for reference in rule change logs, updates, and deletion operations.

key.description: Unique identifier for the business rule, such as 'MAX_POST_LENGTH', 'EDIT_GRACE_PERIOD'. This corresponds directly to the 'key' column. Used throughout the codebase, admin UIs, and logs for referencing a rule.

value.description: The value assigned to the rule, stored as string for flexible typing. Represents the parameter/setting of the rule (e.g., '10000', 'true', etc.). Maps to the 'value' column.

description.description: Human-readable explanation for the business rule, shown in the admin panel and compliance reports. Maps to the 'description' column in the discussionboard_business_rules table. Used for display and policy clarity.

IDiscussionBoardBusinessRules.description:
The canonical schema for a business rule in the Discussion Board platform. Derived from the discussionboard_business_rules model, this type reflects the result of CRUD and search operations on business rules.

Each property is documented for administrative, compliance, and platform extension workflows.

key.description: The unique key for this business rule as described in the requirements (e.g., 'MAX_COMMENT_DEPTH', 'ALLOW_THREAD_LOCKING'). Must be unique across all business rule records. Enforced by schema constraint.

value.description: The stringified value for the business rule, interpreted contextually by business logic. For example, 'false' may mean posts are not editable after submission.

description.description: Textual description of the business rule's purpose and scope. Aids transparency, admin review, and compliance audits.

IDiscussionBoardBusinessRules.ICreate.description: Schema for creating a new business rule in the discussionboard_business_rules table. Reflects atomic, normalized input structure as required by the requirements documentation. Used for administrative configuration and compliance workflow purposes.

key.description: Optional update for the unique key of this rule. Must remain unique. Used when renaming or adjusting referencing across the system.

value.description: Optional updated value for this rule's configuration.

description.description: Optional new description text explaining the rule's business purpose.

IDiscussionBoardBusinessRules.IUpdate.description: Schema for updating an existing business rule in the platform. All properties are optional, allowing partial modification via administrative UIs, bulk update scripts, or compliance operations. Ensures changes can be tracked and properly applied as required by audit logs in the requirements analysis.

INullResult.description: This schema is used for endpoints that return no meaningful data, but indicate successful processing or absence of an entity. For example, deletion operations that require only status codes, not a result object. It is a structural placeholder with no properties.

actor_admin_id.description: Optional. Filter by the admin who performed the policy change. Maps to the 'actor_admin_id' in discussionboard_policy_change_logs.

changed_policy_id.description: Optional. Filter for specific content policy change actions.

changed_rule_id.description: Optional. Filter for business rule change actions.

change_type.description: Optional. Filter by type of change such as 'ADD', 'EDIT', or 'DEACTIVATE'. Application/business logic may implement additional enums as platform evolves.

before_value.description: Optional. Search for logs where the previous value included a specific pattern/text.

after_value.description: Optional. Restrict to logs where new post-change value matches a search string.

changed_at_from.description: Optional. Start timestamp (inclusive) for filtering changes.

page.description: Result page # (for pagination).

limit.description: Page size for paginated responses.

id.description:
고유 식별자입니다. 이 값은 각 비즈니스 규칙 엔트리를 시스템 전체에서 식별하는 데 사용됩니다.

Prisma 스키마에서 각 규칙의 id 칼럼 주석을 참조하세요. 변경 불가하며 각 규칙마다 반드시 존재해야 합니다.

key.description:
비즈니스 규칙의 고유 식별자(예: 'MAX_POST_LENGTH', 'ALLOW_POST_EDITING' 등)입니다.

Prisma 스키마의 key 칼럼 주석과 비즈니스 도메인 상의 용도, 중복 불가 조건을 반영하였습니다. 규칙은 시스템 내에서 상수적으로 참조되므로, 일반적으로 대문자+언더스코어 네이밍이 권장됩니다.

value.description:
실제 비즈니스 규칙의 값입니다. 예를 들어 최대 글자수 '10000', 허용 플래그 'true' 등 다양한 타입(문자/숫자/불리언 형태)이 문자열로 저장됩니다.

Prisma 스키마 value 칼럼 주석 및 플랫폼의 동적 규칙 파라미터화 요구사항을 반영하였습니다. 명확성과 확장성을 위해 항상 atomic string 값이어야 하며, 실제 적용 시 타입 파싱에 유의해야 합니다.

description.description:
이 비즈니스 규칙의 설명/설명문입니다. 시스템 관리자나 사용자에게 규칙의 목적과 의미를 안내하여 투명성과 가독성을 확보합니다.

Prisma 스키마의 description 칼럼 설명과 비즈니스 설명 요구사항에 따라, UI 나 관리도구에서 규칙 설명을 직관적으로 표시할 목적으로 사용됩니다.

DiscussionBoardBusinessRules.description:
게시판 서비스의 비즈니스 규칙 엔터티입니다.

Prisma 스키마 discussionboard_business_rules 테이블에서 정의한 각 비즈니스 규칙에 대한 시스템 전역적 설정을 제공합니다. 예시로, 게시글 최대 길이, 수정/삭제 허용 여부, 각종 플래그 등이 이 엔터티로 저장됩니다.

비즈니스 규칙은 어드민 콘솔, UI 표기, 정책 전달, 법적 감사 등 다양한 용도로 직접 활용되며, audit 로그와 연계해 히스토리 관리(롤백/감사)에 중추적 역할을 수행합니다. 모든 필드는 원자적(atomic)으로 분리되어 저장되므로, Prisma DB 설계 원칙(3NF)을 엄격하게 준수합니다. 변경 시 반드시 PolicyChangeLog, 시스템 감사 로그 등과 연동해 이력 데이터도 남기게 됩니다.

IDiscussionBoardCommentEdit.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching and filtering edits made to discussion board comments. This object enables flexible querying of comment edit logs for audits, rollback, moderation, and UI history panels, as required by business rules.

Properties map directly to searchable columns from the 'discussionboard_comment_edits' table. Filtering enables fine-grained queries on editor, time periods, specific comment, or content after edit. Always supports pagination and ordering info as per standard API conventions. Required fields are minimized to increase search flexibility.

comment_id.description:
Filter by the edited comment's unique identifier (UUID from discussionboard_comments.id). Used for narrowing search to edits for a specific comment.

Useful when reviewing or displaying an edit history in the UI for a specific comment. Optional.

editor_id.description:
Filter by the editor's unique member identifier (UUID from discussionboard_members.id). Limits results to edits performed by a given user.

Supports audit scenarios and personal edit history display. Optional.

created_after.description:
Return only edits created after this timestamp (inclusive). Enables time range searching for compliance or UI windowing.

Example: '2025-05-01T00:00:00Z'. Optional.

created_before.description:
Return only edits created before this timestamp (exclusive). Enables time range searching for moderation review or limited history browsing.

Example: '2025-05-10T00:00:00Z'. Optional.

edit_summary.description:
Search for an edit summary containing this text (case-insensitive substring match). Supports UI search and moderator reasoning workflows.

Example: 'typo' to find all minor correction edits. Optional.

IPageIDiscussionBoardCommentEdit.description: Container object for returning paginated results of comment edit entities, following the standard IPage pattern. Used for UI tables, moderation logs, and compliance dashboards. Aligns with the IPage definition and contains both edit data and pagination metadata.

IDiscussionBoardCommentEdit.description:
Full detail for a single discussion board comment edit event, based on 'discussionboard_comment_edits' schema.

Each record captures an atomic modification to a comment's text, logging what was changed, who made the change, and when. Used for audit trails, rollback, and reviewing moderation actions.

References the related comment, editor, and provides a snapshot of the comment after the edit.

id.description: Primary key - unique identifier for this comment edit.

comment_id.description: Foreign key referencing the edited comment's unique identifier in 'discussionboard_comments.id'. Used for reconstructing edit history.

editor_id.description: References the member who performed this edit (discussionboard_members.id) for accountability and personal histories.

oneOf.description: Short explanation or reason for the edit. E.g., 'corrected typo', used in audit/moderation UIs. Nullable if no summary provided during edit.

edit_summary.description: Short explanation or reason for the edit. E.g., 'corrected typo', used in audit/moderation UIs. Nullable if no summary provided during edit.

body_after_edit.description: Snapshot of the comment's body text after this edit was applied. Required for full rollback and audit flows.

created_at.description: The timestamp when this edit was performed (ISO 8601, UTC). Used for ordering edit histories.

IDiscussionBoardCommentEdit.ICreate.description:
Input required to log a new comment edit event. Used when a comment is edited for audit/compliance tracking. Fields match the normalized structure in 'discussionboard_comment_edits'.

Required by audit, rollback, dispute resolution, and user-facing history features.

comment_id.description: References the comment being edited (discussionboard_comments.id). Required.

editor_id.description: References the member executing the edit (discussionboard_members.id). Required for accountability/audit.

oneOf.description: Optional short summary explaining the reason for the edit. E.g., 'fixed typo'. Nullable, but recommended for moderator or self-edits.

edit_summary.description: Optional short summary explaining the reason for the edit. E.g., 'fixed typo'. Nullable, but recommended for moderator or self-edits.

body_after_edit.description: The revised comment text after editing. Required to capture the state post-edit for rollback/audit.

IDiscussionBoardCommentEdit.IUpdate.description:
Update request for amending an existing comment edit event. Typically restricted to summary or body changes, and only allowed by original editor or moderator by policy.

Allows correction to summary or content within audit-tracked events.

oneOf.description: Updated summary/reason for this edit log. Optional, and may be set to null.

edit_summary.description: Updated summary/reason for this edit log. Optional, and may be set to null.

body_after_edit.description: Corrected or amended content post-edit. Needed for correcting audit log mistakes or extending moderator notes.

IDiscussionBoardPostReaction.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching, filtering, and paginating reactions (likes/dislikes) on posts, as per platform engagement tracking and moderation analysis requirements.

Allows filtering by reaction type, member, post, creation time, and paging options. Matches columns and query logic of 'discussionboard_post_reactions'.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Filters results to reactions made by a specific member (discussionboard_members.id). Optional.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Filters to reactions targeting a single post (discussionboard_posts.id). Optional.

reaction_type.description: Filter by type of reaction. Allowed values: 'like', 'dislike', and platform extensions. See enum EDiscussionBoardReactionType. Optional.

created_after.description: Return reactions created after this timestamp (inclusive). Optional.

created_before.description: Return reactions created before this timestamp (exclusive). Optional.

IPageDiscussionBoardPostReaction.description: Paginated container of post reaction records and result metadata, conforming to the IPage pattern for standardized paging responses across the API.

IDiscussionBoardPostReaction.description:
Represents a single like/dislike (or similar) reaction for a discussion board post, as stored in 'discussionboard_post_reactions'.

Captures the member, target post, type of reaction, and audit timestamps. Used for engagement metrics, UI state, and platform moderation.

id.description: Primary key for this post reaction record.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Foreign key reference to the member making the reaction (discussionboard_members.id).

discussionboard_post_id.description: Foreign key to the post receiving reaction (discussionboard_posts.id).

reaction_type.description: Type of reaction, e.g., 'like', 'dislike'. Platform may extend with more, but must enumerate allowed values.

created_at.description: Timestamp of reaction creation (ISO 8601) for auditing and analytics.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of soft-deletion/undo for reversibility and audit trail. Null if active.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp of soft-deletion/undo for reversibility and audit trail. Null if active.

IDiscussionBoardPostReaction.ICreate.description:
Input required to create a new reaction to a post (e.g., like/dislike) by an authenticated member. Enforces key business logic: unique reaction per user/post pair and enum type validity.

Required for all engagement and analytics workflows.

reaction_type.description: The type of reaction to record. Allowed values: 'like', 'dislike' (see EDiscussionBoardReactionType).

IDiscussionBoardPostReaction.IUpdate.description:
Request to update an existing post reaction record (e.g., to switch between like/dislike, or correct error). Usually restricted to original member or moderator role.

Direct mapping to allowed update fields in 'discussionboard_post_reactions'.

reaction_type.description: Updated reaction type. Allowed: 'like', 'dislike' (platform may extend). Changing this supports correcting errors or user updates.

IDiscussionBoardCommentReaction.IRequest.description:
Request object for searching/filtering comment reactions (likes/dislikes) on the platform. Targeted for engagement analytics and moderation review workflows, mapped to 'discussionboard_comment_reactions' structure.

Allows filtering by member, comment, type, or timestamps with paging info.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Filter to reactions from this member only (discussionboard_members.id). Optional.

discussionboard_comment_id.description: Filter to reactions for a specific comment only (discussionboard_comments.id). Optional.

reaction_type.description: Reaction type to filter by. Allowed values: 'like', 'dislike', etc. See EDiscussionBoardReactionType. Optional.

created_after.description: Return records after this timestamp (inclusive). Optional.

created_before.description: Return records before this timestamp (exclusive). Optional.

IPageDiscussionBoardCommentReaction.description: Standard paging result type for returning lists of comment reaction objects, conforming to IPage<T> conventions across the platform API.

IDiscussionBoardCommentReaction.description:
Represents a single reaction (like/dislike) made by a member on a particular comment, as logged in 'discussionboard_comment_reactions'.

Used for engagement metrics, sentiment tracking, and moderation workflows. Each row records member, comment, reaction type, and audit/soft-delete info.

id.description: Primary key, unique identifier for this comment reaction object.

discussionboard_member_id.description: The member who made this reaction. FK to discussionboard_members.id.

discussionboard_comment_id.description: The comment receiving this reaction. FK to discussionboard_comments.id.

reaction_type.description: The type of reaction (like/dislike). Allowed values enforced by platform; see EDiscussionBoardReactionType. Extension possible.

created_at.description: Time when the reaction was made (ISO 8601 UTC).

oneOf.description: When the reaction was deleted/undone. Null if still active. Supports audit/undo/compliance.

deleted_at.description: When the reaction was deleted/undone. Null if still active. Supports audit/undo/compliance.

IPage.IPagination.description: Page information for IPage<T> containers. Indicates current page, page limits, and overall result context. Used for UI pagination, analytics, and navigation.

limit.description:
Number of records per page.

Defaults to 100 if omitted.

records.description: Total records matching the query in the dataset.

IPage.IRequest.description: Standardized request object for paginated queries. Commonly included as a nested object in all <IRequest> filter payloads allowing client to specify what page, size, and sort they want.

oneOf.description: Which page of results to fetch (1-based). May be null for default.
Which page of results to fetch (1-based). May be null for default.

page.description: Which page of results to fetch (1-based). May be null for default.

oneOf.description: Maximum results per page. Usually defaults to 100. Null to use default.
Maximum results per page. Usually defaults to 100. Null to use default.

limit.description: Maximum results per page. Usually defaults to 100. Null to use default.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the page of moderation appeals.

This includes information such as the current page number, limit per page, total records, and total pages. Originates from the IPage standard interface. It enables clients to handle result navigation according to user preferences and UI requirements.

data.description:
Array of moderation appeal objects on this page.

Each entry refers to a single moderation appeal according to the schema for IDiscussionBoardModerationAppeal. This array comprises the results of the query for the current page.

IPageDiscussionBoardModerationAppeal.description:
Paginated result containing moderation appeal records for the Discussion Board platform.

Fulfills list rendering, search, and management use cases in moderation and admin panels. Returns both the standard IPage pagination metadata and the data array of moderation appeal objects according to the IDiscussionBoardModerationAppeal schema.

See also: Standard IPage documentation for pagination structure.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique ID for the moderation appeal record.

References the unique appeal identifier in the moderation workflow. Used for traceability and audit of each appeal filed by users.

moderation_action_id.description: References the moderation action being appealed against. Points to the moderation action record in the system.

member_id.description: The ID of the member appealing the moderation action. Links to the actor making the appeal.

appeal_reason.description:
Text provided by the member explaining the grounds for the appeal.

Reflects the user's rationale or argument for contesting the moderation action. Mandatory for transparent review.

appeal_status.description:
Current status of the appeal process.

Examples include: 'pending', 'under_review', 'decided', 'withdrawn' according to workflow configuration.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the appeal was submitted.

Used for chronological ordering and deadline enforcement.

last_updated_at.description:
The last modification timestamp for the appeal record.

Reflects when any part of this appeal record was most recently changed (content, status, etc).

IDiscussionBoardModerationAppeal.description:
A record representing a formal request by a member to challenge or contest a prior moderation action.

Defined to support the dispute, review, and escalation procedures as described in the platform's moderation policy documents. Captures user rationale, tracking information, and workflow state for each processed moderation appeal.

moderation_action_id.description: Specifies the moderation action that is being appealed. References the ID of the moderation action to which the user's appeal pertains.

member_id.description: ID of the member submitting this appeal. Every appeal must be tied to a member account.

appeal_reason.description:
Rationale or explanation the member provides for their appeal.

Required for proper review, decision-making, and compliance with dispute management rules.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAppeal.ICreate.description:
The request payload for submitting a new moderation appeal in the Discussion Board system.

Must include which moderation action is being challenged, the appealing member's ID, and the user's explanation for the appeal. Designed for the IDiscussionBoardModerationAppeal creation API endpoint.

appeal_reason.description: The new reason or rationale provided by the member for the appeal. Used if the member modifies or expands on their case before a decision is reached.

appeal_status.description: Updated status for the appeal, e.g., 'withdrawn', as per workflow configuration.

DiscussionBoardModerationAppeal.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for a moderation appeal in the Discussion Board system.

Allows changes to the appeal reason (by the member) or to the appeal status (only to withdraw, before a final decision). This is referenced by the API endpoint for updating an appeal record.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the moderation appeal entity.

Serves as the primary key for query, audit, and linkage to further workflow records.

moderation_action_id.description: Foreign key reference to the moderation action that is being appealed.

member_id.description: Foreign key to the member who submitted the appeal.

appeal_reason.description: The detailed reason or text the user submitted for justification of their appeal.

appeal_status.description: Current appeal status, such as 'pending', 'under_review', 'withdrawn', or 'decided'. Indicates where in the workflow this appeal currently is.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when this appeal was created.

last_updated_at.description: Most recent timestamp for changes to this entity.

DiscussionBoardModerationAppeal.description: Full entity schema for a moderation appeal in the Discussion Board platform. Used for API responses containing all detailed fields tracked for this workflow entity.

appeal_id.description: ID of the moderation appeal for which decisions are to be queried.

moderator_id.description: Filter for decisions made by a specific moderator (nullable, only if filtering by moderator responsibility).

admin_id.description: Filter for decisions made by a specific admin (nullable).

decision_outcome.description: Outcome to filter by, such as 'upheld', 'overturned', 'modified', as determined by workflow requirements.

created_after.description: Include only decisions created after this timestamp (optional filtering).

created_before.description: Include only decisions created before this timestamp (optional filtering).

page.description: Zero-based page index for pagination (optional); defaults to 0.

limit.description: Results per page for pagination (optional).

DiscussionBoardAppealDecision.IRequest.description:
Request search/filter parameters for retrieving a paginated, filtered list of moderation appeal decisions.

May include specific appeal_id, moderator/admin IDs, outcome status, creation time window, and standard pagination controls.

pagination.description: Paging and result count metadata for returned appeal decision summary.

data.description: List array of appeal decision entries for the specified page, following full schema for DiscussionBoardAppealDecision.

PageDiscussionBoardAppealDecision.description:
Paginated collection of moderation appeal decision entries as found in the Discussion Board.

Returned by search or filter APIs for appeal resolution and review purposes, incorporating standard IPage pagination.

id.description: Primary key for the moderation appeal decision entity.

appeal_id.description: Foreign key reference to the appeal being decided upon.

moderator_id.description: ID for the moderator making the decision (nullable if made by admin).

admin_id.description: ID for the admin making the decision (nullable if made by moderator).

decision_outcome.description: Final outcome of the appeal, such as 'upheld', 'overturned', 'modified', or 'escalated'. Enum values depend on business logic.

decision_rationale.description: Explanation or reasoning for the decision outcome regarding the moderation appeal.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the decision was made.

DiscussionBoardAppealDecision.description:
Entity schema for recording outcomes and rationales for moderation appeal decisions.

Tracks moderator/admin responsibility, detailed outcome, rationale, and precise timing as required for workflows and audit compliance.

appeal_id.description: ID of the appeal to be decided upon. Must reference an existing open appeal.

moderator_id.description: ID of the moderator responsible for this decision (nullable, if decided by admin).

admin_id.description: ID of the admin responsible for this decision (nullable, if decided by moderator).

decision_outcome.description: Outcome determined by the reviewer, such as 'upheld', 'overturned', etc. Strictly controlled values per platform policy.

decision_rationale.description: Text rationale explaining the logic, policy, and evidence considered when making decision.

DiscussionBoardAppealDecision.ICreate.description:
Request payload to create a new moderation appeal decision entry.

Must include the target appeal, the chosen outcome, and a complete rationale. Optional assignment to moderator/admin determines responsibility.

decision_outcome.description: New or corrected outcome for the appeal decision, as allowed by workflow policy (edit/clarify outcome before notification/closure).

decision_rationale.description: Updated rationale text for the appeal decision; typically used for clarification.

DiscussionBoardAppealDecision.IUpdate.description: Update request for an appeal decision entity. Modifies the outcome or rationale of an existing record, subject to policy for allowed changes.

recipient_member_id.description: ID of the intended notification recipient (for querying current actor's notifications).

read.description: Whether to filter by read/unread status.

delivered_after.description: Return only notification entries delivered after this timestamp (optional).

delivered_before.description: Return only notification entries delivered before this timestamp (optional).

page.description: Zero-based page index for pagination.

limit.description: Limit the number of records per page.

DiscussionBoardNotification.IRequest.description:
Search parameters for listing or filtering notifications for a recipient via API.

Allows filtering by recipient, notification type, read status, delivery date window, and supports pagination controls for efficient dashboard display.

pagination.description: Structural data for pagination of notification results, as standardized by IPage.

data.description: Array of discussion board notification objects for the specified page.

PageDiscussionBoardNotification.description:
Paginated result of discussion board notification records for notification center or API feeds.

Combines paging metadata and an array of notification records built from the DiscussionBoardNotification schema.

id.description: Primary key for the notification entry in the system.

recipient_member_id.description: The ID of the user/member receiving the notification.

trigger_actor_id.description: Optional ID for the user/admin/mod who triggered the notification event.

target_post_id.description: If present, the notification is linked to a post entity with this ID.

target_comment_id.description: If present, the notification is linked to a comment entity with this ID.

target_report_id.description: If present, the notification relates to a report entity (moderation/report event).

target_section_id.description: If present, the notification is about a section (may be report, move, assignment, etc.).

delivered_at.description: Timestamp marking when notification was delivered to the user.

read_at.description: Timestamp when the notification was read (nullable, means unread if null).

created_at.description: Timestamp for notification entry creation (for sorting/audit).

DiscussionBoardNotification.description:
Entity representing an in-system notification for a Discussion Board user.

Captures recipient, event context, type, linkages to content/reports, delivery/read timestamp, and audit trail fields.

operations.specification: Discussion Board Channel list and search endpoint. Returns paginated channels and may accept filters like name or description. Associated with the 'discussionboard_channels' table in the Prisma DB schema. Required for systematic grouping and management of all discussion venues as per requirements analysis.
operations.description:
This operation provides a paginated list of discussion board channels, supporting optional search and filter criteria on fields such as name or description. Only non-deleted and active channels are included in normal queries, reflecting the underlying rules documented in the Prisma schema regarding soft delete tracking and normalization. Access is typically available to authenticated users with at least 'member' role, as channels must be discoverable by the general user base (see user journeys and access control matrix).

Channels represent logical groupings under which sections and, subsequently, boards and posts are organized. This design supports scalability, business partitioning, and administrative audit, addressing requirements from both business and technical analysis. This endpoint may be used by administrators for oversight or by regular users for board navigation.

Consumers should anticipate standard pagination, sorting (e.g., by creation date), and error handling if filter parameters are malformed. Soft-deleted channels will only be visible when administrative filters are enabled. Strict role and access controls apply when requesting deleted channels or sensitive metadata. See also related endpoints for channel detail, creation, update, and removal.
operations.summary: Retrieves a paginated and searchable list of discussion board channels from the 'discussionboard_channels' table.

requestBody.description: Optional search, pagination, and filter parameters for channel listing.

responseBody.description: Paginated result containing discussion board channel summary objects.

operations.specification: Retrieves the details of a specific discussion board channel. Tied to the 'discussionboard_channels' table in Prisma DB, supports channel administration and navigation.
operations.description:
Fetches a single discussion board channel entity by its unique identifier. This endpoint exposes all essential attributes such as channel name, description, creation time, update time, and soft-deletion status (if applicable). The purpose is to display channel-level metadata to either administrative interfaces or regular users interested in viewing or joining the channel.

The endpoint enforces strict compliance with access rules from the requirements documentation: all users may read public channels, but only moderators/admins may see non-active, deleted, or hidden channels. Security checks are required to enforce access level and audit trail requirements. The operation operates directly on atomic, normalized data as defined in the Prisma DB schema, guaranteeing consistency with system-of-record values.

Related endpoints provide means to create, update, or delete channels. Standard error responses are issued if the identifier is not found or if access is denied.
operations.summary: Returns detailed information for the designated channel from the 'discussionboard_channels' table.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the channel to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Detailed representation of the specified channel entity.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion board channel. Storage and validation are based on the 'discussionboard_channels' table in the DB schema.
operations.description:
Allows an administrative user to define and register a new logical grouping for discussion board content (channel). The API accepts channel configuration data such as name, description, and metadata in accordance with business requirements. Consistency with existing channels is enforced—name must be unique as per schema constraint. Timestamps for creation and update are auto-managed, and the new channel is initialized in non-deleted, active state.

Only users with administrative privileges are authorized. All input is validated against 3NF normalization rules (atomic values only, no derived or aggregated data). On conflict (e.g., duplicate channel name), an error with corresponding code is returned. Upon success, the newly created channel entity is provided in response.

Business rules and audit requirements dictate that channel creation is logged, and new channels are discoverable by default unless specified otherwise. See also channel update and deletion endpoints for further modifications.
operations.summary: Registers a new channel record in the 'discussionboard_channels' table (admin only).

requestBody.description: New channel initialization data conforming to system requirements.

responseBody.description: The created channel entity with populated metadata fields.

operations.specification: Update an existing discussion board channel configuration or metadata. Linked directly to the 'discussionboard_channels' table.
operations.description:
Modifies an existing logical grouping (channel) on the platform by channel unique identifier. Only allowed for administrative users. This endpoint enforces all business requirements regarding channel uniqueness, naming conventions, and normalization rules as per Prisma DB schema. Updates to fields like name, description, or soft-deletion timestamp are supported, and the updated entity is returned in the response.

The update action is logged for audit purposes in accordance with business policy. Concurrency controls and validation errors (e.g., for duplicate names) are handled strictly to prevent data corruption. Only authorized administrators may execute this action; regular members or moderators are forbidden. Updatability is restricted to atomic channel attributes as specified in DB schema comments.

The client must provide details: post to attach the comment, thread (root or child), author, comment body, nesting depth, and optional metadata. Business rules enforce content guidelines (see policies/rules tables), required presence of referenced post/thread/author, and context-sensitive restrictions (delete permissions, post-locked exclusion, etc).

Moderation logic: If the target post is locked, comment is rejected. Comments may be staged for review depending on board settings. Upon success, a fully-populated comment object is returned. Soft deletion and edit status defaults handled at creation. Permission errors, missing references, or invalid request bodies produce error/validation responses. Matches discussionboard_comments schema.

operations.description:
This operation updates a moderation appeal record from the discussionboard_moderation_appeals table by its unique ID. It is primarily intended for use by the appeal's owner (the member who filed the appeal), allowing them to modify the appeal reason, withdraw an unresolved appeal, or otherwise update information on record as long as the appeal status is still 'pending' or 'under_review'. Once a decision has been made (appeal_status is 'decided', 'resolved', etc.), updates are no longer permitted. The endpoint enforces security checks to guarantee that only the original filer or authorized moderators/admins may perform updates, as defined by the platform's business rules and role matrix in the requirements analysis.

The request body must follow the DiscussionBoardModerationAppeal.IUpdate interface, specifying only the mutable fields (e.g., appeal_reason, appeal_status if withdrawing). The endpoint does not allow altering immutable audit columns or changing the member or action the appeal refers to. On success, the response returns the updated DiscussionBoardModerationAppeal entity, reflecting the post-update state. Errors return standard API error types for not found, forbidden, or invalid update attempts. Any field changes are logged according to platform audit policy.

Related: Creating new appeals uses POST; retrieving details uses GET. Decisions on appeals use a separate endpoint for appeal decisions. Rollbacks or admin overrides are handled via the moderation panel, not this endpoint.
